spark.title: How to Prepare for Code Comprehension Rounds
spark.summary: Navigate unfamiliar multi-file codebases under time pressure: map entry points, trace data/state mutations, catch concurrency or logic bugs, and write safe fixes with tests.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, read top-down from the public entry point and tests first—never read every helper line-by-line before building a mental map of state ownership and side effects.

concept.whyItMatters: Modern engineering loops increasingly replace pure LeetCode trivia with **Code Comprehension & Debugging** rounds where you inherit a realistic 300–1,000 line service with subtle race conditions, memory leaks, off-by-one pagination bugs, or broken retry logic.
whenToUse: Code review, debugging, and codebase comprehension interviews.
Onboarding onto an unfamiliar production service or triaging an active incident.
whenNotToUse: Rewriting the entire codebase from scratch instead of diagnosing the root cause and applying a minimal, tested fix.
keyPoints: Step 1 (Entry-Point & Test Scan, 5m): Locate `main`/routes/controllers and existing unit tests to see intended contracts.
Step 2 (Data Flow & State Map, 10m): Trace where inputs enter, where state is mutated, and where external I/O (DB/cache/network) happens.
Step 3 (Bug Hunt Checklist): Check boundary conditions (`<` vs `<=`), shared mutable state without locks, unclosed resources, swallowed exceptions, and N+1 loops.
Step 4 (Reproduce -> Fix -> Verify): Write a failing reproduction test first, apply the minimal fix, and confirm all existing + new tests pass.

sections.content:
## Preparation & Execution Matrix

| Bug Category | Common Symptom in Code | Fix Strategy |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Concurrency** | Check-then-act on shared `dict`/`Map` | Atomic CAS, lock, or thread-safe collection |
| **Pagination / Offset** | Missing/duplicate items on concurrent writes | Keyset (cursor) pagination instead of `OFFSET` |
| **Resource Leak** | Unclosed streams/connections on exception | `with` context manager (Python) / `try-with-resources` (Java) |
| **Retry Storm** | Immediate tight-loop retries on 5xx | Exponential backoff + jitter + max attempts |

steps.title: Normal Path
steps.explanation: Caller sends work to Router / API (Normal Path).

steps.title: Core Execution
steps.explanation: Router / API coordinates with Processor while preserving the core invariant (Core Execution).

steps.title: Contention / Fault
steps.explanation: Under load skew or dependency lag, State Layer absorbs pressure without cascading (Contention / Fault).

steps.title: Steady Convergence
steps.explanation: The system stabilizes cleanly within its latency and correctness budget (Steady Convergence).

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement How To Prepare For Code Comprehension without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, read top-down from the public entry point and tests first—never read every helper line-by-line before building a mental map of state ownership and side effects.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When How To Prepare For Code Comprehension experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.
